Understanding Open Zoning in Larimer County

Christine Gwinnup – Northern Colorado Listing Specialist


Open zoning—also known as zoning code "O"—is one of Larimer County’s most flexible (and misunderstood) land designations. It’s often found in western Larimer County near the foothills, rural areas, and environmentally sensitive zones.

What Does Open Zoning Actually Mean?

Open zoning allows for low-density rural living. It’s not the wild west—but it does offer more flexibility than other residential zones. That said, it comes with key restrictions you need to understand before buying or subdividing land.

  • Typically allows single-family homes and accessory buildings
  • Does not allow dense development or multi-unit housing without special approval
  • Agriculture and animals may be permitted with limits

Pro tip: Open zoning isn’t a free pass—it’s a structured designation with specific limitations, especially regarding density, road access, and water/septic requirements.

Can You Subdivide Open Zoned Land?

Maybe—but it’s not easy. Density limitations often require 10–35 acres per home. You may need a complex subdivision review process and must meet rural standards for road access, utilities, and water rights.

Do I Need Permits or Reviews?

If you're planning anything beyond a primary residence—such as an event venue, commercial use, or even some home-based businesses—you'll likely need:

  • A Special Review Permit
  • County hearings and public input
  • Conditional Use or Use by Right confirmation

Well, Septic, ILCs & More

Buying land means understanding more than just zoning. Here are must-know resources:

  • How to Read a Colorado Well Permit
